title: Broadband Black Friday deals 2026 UK: the true cost of each deal
description: Broadband Black Friday deals 2026: Virgin 264Mb from £18.99, Vodafone 5G with a £160 voucher, and the real 24-month cost. Checked 7 November 2026.
intro:
**The best-value fixed-line broadband deal we can confirm today is Virgin Media's M250 at £18.99 a month on a 24-month contract, with average speeds of 264Mb and no setup fee.** Its yearly £4 rises take the average cost to about £23.32 a month over the contract, which is still well under the typical full-fibre price.

Broadband Black Friday deals are already showing on comparison sites, and providers usually keep them running until Cyber Monday on 30 November. If your contract has ended, you're probably overpaying now, so it's worth switching rather than waiting. Prices were checked on Uswitch's broadband listings on 7 November 2026.

deals.name: Virgin Media M250 Fibre Broadband, 264Mb, 24 months
deals.note: No setup cost. Rises by £4 a month each April, so the average over 24 months is about £23.32. Fast enough for a busy household streaming in 4K.

deals.name: Virgin Media M500 Fibre Broadband, 516Mb, 24 months
deals.note: Twice the speed of M250 for £3 more a month. Averages about £26.32 a month once the April rises are added. Good for big households and gamers.

deals.name: Virgin Media Gig1 Fibre Broadband, 1000Mb, 24 months
deals.note: Gigabit speeds for only £5 more than M250, averaging about £28.32 a month over the contract. Most homes won't notice the difference over M500, but it's cheap for what it is.

deals.name: Vodafone 5G Broadband, 50Mb, 24 months + £160 voucher
deals.note: Home broadband over the 5G mobile network, with no line needed. Rises £3.50 each April. Take off the £160 voucher and it works out at about £10 a month. Only worth it with strong 5G signal at home.

deals.name: Sky Superfast Broadband, 67Mb, 24 months
deals.note: No setup cost and up to £200 credit if you're leaving another provider early. Sky says the price may rise during the contract but doesn't give an amount, so ask before ordering.

deals.name: NOW Superfast Broadband, 67Mb, 24 months + £70 voucher
deals.note: Sky's budget brand, on the same network. The £70 voucher takes about £3 a month off, but Virgin's M250 is faster for less.

deals.name: Virgin Media M500 Entertainment + Netflix, 516Mb, 24 months
deals.note: Tagged as a Black Friday deal: broadband, 150+ channels and Netflix, plus up to £300 credit if you're leaving another contract early. Rises £4 each April.

deals.name: BT Fibre Essential, 36Mb, 24 months
deals.note: Slow and dear by comparison, and it rises £4 every March, averaging about £32.66 a month. Only for people who must stay with BT; wait for a better Black Friday offer.

body:
## How broadband Black Friday deals work

Broadband providers don't usually slash prices for one day. Instead, they cut the monthly price on a 24-month contract, add a voucher or bill credit, or waive setup fees, and run the offer for several weeks. Uswitch was already flagging Black Friday broadband, TV and phone deals in early November, and these normally carry on until Cyber Monday on 30 November.

The key point: because you pay every month for two years, a £3-a-month saving is worth £72. That's often more than you'd save on a TV.

## How to work out the real cost

The headline price is only the start. To compare deals properly:

**1. Add the yearly price rises.** Since January 2025, Ofcom has made providers set out mid-contract rises in pounds and pence. Virgin Media adds £4 a month every April and BT adds £4 every March. Vodafone's 5G Broadband rises £3.50 each April. Sky and NOW say prices may rise but don't put a figure on the Uswitch listing, so check before you sign.

**2. Take off vouchers and credit.** A £160 voucher on a 24-month deal is worth about £6.67 a month. Early switch credit (up to £200 or £300 on some deals above) only helps if you're paying a fee to leave your current provider.

**3. Add setup and upfront fees.** All the deals above have no setup cost, but some ask for a £5 advance fee that's credited back to your account.

We've worked out the average monthly cost for the deals where the rises are known, assuming you start in November 2026.

## What speed do you need?

- **Under 70Mb:** fine for one or two people browsing and streaming in HD.
- **250Mb to 500Mb:** the sweet spot for families, 4K streaming and working from home.
- **900Mb and up:** only worth paying extra for if you move huge files or have lots of heavy users at once.

Speeds quoted here are the average speeds providers must advertise. Check what's available at your address on a comparison site, as Virgin Media's cable network doesn't reach every home.

## Target prices for Black Friday 2026

Uswitch's figures put the average starting price of a full-fibre deal at about £28 a month. Based on today's listings, good prices to aim for are:

- **Around 70Mb:** under £22 a month.
- **250Mb to 500Mb:** under £22 a month, or an average under £27 once rises are counted.
- **900Mb to 1Gb:** under £25 a month to start.

If your current bill is well above these and your contract has ended, switch now. Out-of-contract customers usually pay much more than new customers.

## How to switch

Since September 2024, switching between most broadband networks uses Ofcom's One Touch Switch system. You just sign up with the new provider and it handles the move and cancels your old service. You don't need to call your old provider, and you get 14 days to cancel a new contract if you change your mind.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are broadband deals cheaper on Black Friday?

Often, but not by much. The Black Friday offers are usually a lower monthly price, a voucher or bill credit, and they tend to start in early November. A good deal you see now is unlikely to be beaten by much on 27 November.

### When do broadband Black Friday deals end?

Most run until Cyber Monday, 30 November 2026, and some last into December. Providers can pull an offer at any time, so don't count on it.

### Do I have to pay to leave my current contract?

Only if you're still in your minimum term. If so, check whether the new provider offers early switch credit. Sky and Virgin Media both offer up to £200 or £300 on some deals today.

### Is 5G home broadband any good?

It can be, if you get a strong 5G signal indoors. It needs no landline or engineer and is often cheap, but speeds can vary through the day. Vodafone's deal is a good price if your postcode has strong coverage.

### Will my price go up during the contract?

Usually. Virgin Media, BT and Vodafone set out fixed yearly rises in pounds. Look for the rise on the listing and add it into the total cost before you choose.
